answer: Registration deposit scales superlinearly with the live identity count: account n locks capital growing faster than n, so k clones cost on the order of k squared while their capture stays linear and the marginal clone turns ruinous. Honest operators barely feel it: the lock is refundable at exit, a velvet cost rather than a burn, and one marble-solid identity still clears the bar. Paying pro rata to refundable stake reinforces this: equal capital earns more in one proven account than split thin. A sybil budget does not vanish; it drains into karst limestone through holes that never pay back.
